name: Will-o'-the-Wisp Loop
description: The club's gentle night out: along the River Rothay, around the Under Loughrigg lane and back over the stone footbridge, with lights flickering on the water the whole way. Barely a climb worth naming, though the two short rises past Fox How will still make you jump. Runnable end to end in road shoes, and the route we use for the All Hallows' Run.

name: Lantern Terrace Circuit
startPoint: White Moss car park, between Rydal and Grasmere
description: A proper little circuit with one honest pull up to Loughrigg's summit cairn, then the terrace path with the lights of Grasmere laid out below. The drop past Rydal Cave is steep and loose, and the cave has a habit of echoing back footsteps that are not yours. Trail shoes and a strong headtorch after rain.

name: Witching Hour Wansfell
description: Up the stone steps out of town and onto Wansfell Pike the direct way — half an hour of proper climbing in the dark — then over the top and down through Troutbeck's lanes and Skelghyll Woods, where the owls are louder than the runners. On a clear night the moon lays a silver road down the length of Windermere.

name: Headless Horseshoe
description: The classic horseshoe over eight named tops: up by Nab Scar and Heron Pike, along the ridge to Fairfield's broad summit plateau, then back over Hart Crag, Dove Crag and the Pikes. After dark it is easy to lose your head for navigation — the plateau is featureless in mist. Full fell kit, a spare torch and a running partner, no exceptions.

name: All Hallows' Long Round
description: Our long steady one: valley tracks and bridleways linking Elterwater, Great Langdale, Little Langdale and Skelwith. Nothing steep and nowhere technical — just honest distance, with the Langdale Pikes looming black against the stars the whole way round. Two sensible exit points if the night stops being fun.
